issues.original: If your current site covers this list well on a phone, you are already ahead of most restaurants. If it doesn't, that is the work, and it is usually smaller than owners expect.
issues.replacement: If your current site covers this list well on a phone, you have the essentials in place. If it doesn't, that is the work, and it is usually smaller than owners expect.
issues.reason: Unsupported comparative claim ('ahead of most restaurants'); narrow to covering essentials.

issues.original: For a growing share of guests this is the deciding factor, not a nice extra.
issues.replacement: For many guests, this is the deciding factor, not a nice extra.
issues.reason: Unsupported empirical claim about a 'growing share'; narrowed to 'many guests'.

issues.original: Hours are the most searched fact about most local restaurants, and the easiest to get wrong.
issues.replacement: Hours are one of the first things guests check on a local restaurant website, and they are easy to get wrong.
issues.reason: Unsupported empirical claim ('most searched fact'); reframed as importance and ease of error.

assessment.intent: Practical, opinionated guide for independent restaurant owners on what a website needs to do to convert hungry searchers into guests.
assessment.specificity: Good: gives a concrete checklist, a sample four-page architecture, and specific HTML-versus-PDF menu advice.
assessment.evidence: Grounded in Michael's stated restaurant-design approach, plus two credible sources (Google Business Profile special hours, W3C WAI first-review accessibility checks). No invented stats or fake case studies.
assessment.voice: On target: connected conversational sentences, answer-first H2s, Canadian spelling, no corporate padding or smug contrasts, clear explanations before using terms.
assessment.usefulAsset: Yes. A restaurant owner can open their site on a phone and act on this today. Three factual overreach fixes were made; otherwise draft is solid.
